title: What ihram forbids
hookLine: no perfume, no cutting hair, no hunting, no quarrelling

cards: A pilgrim is standing at Arafah with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when his mount throws him. He falls and dies there, still in his two white cloths. The report is in Sahih al-Bukhari.
The people around him turn to the Prophet: what now? His instructions are short. Wash him with water and lote leaves.
Shroud him in his two cloths. No perfume. Don't cover his head.

Then the reason: he'll be raised on the Day of Resurrection still calling out the pilgrim's cry. Even death, in this story, doesn't take him out of ihram. Today, what that state holds a person back from.

teach.b: First, the body. Once a pilgrim is in ihram, some ordinary things stop. No perfume, on the skin or the cloth.

No cutting hair: the Qur'an tells pilgrims not to shave their heads until the offering has reached its place, so the haircut becomes part of the ending, not the middle. Scholars add nails to the same list.

The Qur'an says plainly, in surah five, that wild game is not to be killed on the pilgrimage. A person who might hunt at home lets the animals of the sanctuary be. Third, the tongue, and this one surprises people.

In surah two, Pickthall's translation reads: "there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage." You met that verse back on day three hundred fifty-four. Not just no fighting.
No angry conversation. A crowd, the heat, the lines, the lost luggage, an elbow in the ribs, and the instruction is: don't argue. Of everything on the list, that one asks the most patience.
Fourth, what the rules are for. Each is something small and ordinary, a scent, a trim, a sharp word. None of them is wrong at home.
In ihram, they're set down for a while. The two cloths are what people see.

teach.h: THE RESTRAINT GOES ALL THE WAY DOWN.
teach.b: The restraint is what they don't see, and it goes all the way down. That's why the man who fell at Arafah was left unperfumed and bareheaded. The rules weren't a costume he could take off.
They were the state he was in, and he stayed in it.

how: Pilgrims in ihram avoid perfume, cutting hair and nails, hunting, marital relations and quarreling until the rites release them; the details and the remedy for a slip are set out in each school of Islamic law.

o: perfume, haircuts, hunting and quarrels, set down in ihram
any clothing that isn't pure white, for men and women
food and water from dawn until the sun goes down

games.q: what ihram forbids — tap the pairs.

s: ihram only rules out bad things
it sets down ordinary things too: perfume, a haircut, hunting.
the Qur'an forbids angry conversation on the pilgrimage
surah two: "no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage."
the pilgrim who died at Arafah was perfumed for burial
the Prophet said not to perfume him or cover his head.

games.q: a pilgrim in ihram falls from his mount at Arafah and dies. the people ask the Prophet how to prepare him. what does he say?
o: perfume him and shroud him in new cloth.
wash him, shroud him in his two cloths, no perfume, head uncovered.
send him home to be buried in his own clothes.
games.why: he is left in the state of ihram, and the Prophet says he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection still calling the pilgrim's cry.

practice: Choose one small, ordinary habit to set down for a while, not something bad: your usual scent, checking the score, having the last word. Picture the moment it will reach for you, and picture letting it pass.
If you pray, ask for help in your own words or with a verse you know; if not, just hold the picture and breathe.

wordCard.voice: What ihram forbids. Perfume, cutting hair, hunting, and quarreling, set down while the pilgrim is in the sacred state. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: restraint is the dress. Small things, set down on purpose. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.q: there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage.
